text.p: On overnight commodity markets, copper prices jumped ahead in London to a new 8 and 1/2 month high as fears of further market tightness kept the market on the boil.
Wheat prices fell as players spooked by the size of a corn-led rally took profits.
Gold prices firmed again overnight, as did oil prices.
The CRB Index was up 0.87 points at 241.40.
Copper managed to hold on to most of its heady gains on Wednesday afternoon as fears of further tightness kept the market on the boil.
Three months copper finished the afternoon kerb at $2,340 per tonne, off its 8-1/2 month high of $2,360 touched in the morning but up a respectable $54 on the day.
The premium of cash over three months metal firmed about $10 to $85/7. In addition, the option market saw a boost in activity from Wednesday's spike, traders said.
Many of the other metals took a ride on copper's coat-tails.

Zinc notched up a fresh two-year high of $1,235, coming within a whisker of the January 1995 peak of $1,239. Another burst of fund buying could take it through there, but chartists noted the 14-day RSI was in overbought territory at 74.
The market ended the day $17 higher at $1,230.
Aluminium tried to cement its foothold back above $1,600, finishing at $1,604, up $20. The next major resistance area was seen at $1,620, traders and analysts said.
Nickel leapt $255 to end at $7,910, but the market looked vulnerable, a chartist said.
Lead gained $13 to $670 and tin closed unchanged at $6,065.

Late commission house selling drove CBOT wheat futures to mostly lower closes, with the market still rattled by Tuesday's near-limit-up surge in corn and rally in soybeans, traders said. Wheat traders in Chicago, Kansas City and Minneapolis agreed the real key to near-term rallies or breaks in wheat were tied to corn and soybean futures. Wednesday, it appeared funds were settling down a bit as demand for corn futures waned in late dealings. That triggered selling by locals in corn which touched off a wave of fund long long liquidation in soybeans. Wheat broke amid that uncertainty. Wheat closed 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 1/2 higher, with March down 4-3/4 at $3.59-1/2 a bushel.

New York precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday on light volumes, but the recovery in gold prices continued for a sixth day. "There were no fireworks on the expiry of the March silver and gold options last Friday which may have disappointed some traders," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said. COMEX April gold up 70 cents at $348.40, with $350 seen as resistance, after six day recovery from three year lows.

NYMEX oil prices were firm but off from their highs Wednesday in late afternoon trade after prompt crude failed at technical resistance. "Crude is off from its high because it failed once again at $22.75," said Tom Bentz, analyst with ING Derivatives in New York. March crude was 19 cents higher at $22.71 a barrel. The market's reaction was muted to news China's top leader Deng Xiaoping had died.
